subject: obstetrics-gynaecology
title: Magnesium Sulphate: Pritchard, Zuspan and Toxicity

steps.tx: The anticonvulsant of choice for eclampsia prevention and treatment is **magnesium sulphate**. It outperforms diazepam and phenytoin in preventing recurrent fits. Every labour ward stocks it with its antidote immediately available. Careful history taking and examination help place this finding in the right clinical context before treatment is planned.
steps.say: Magnesium sulphate is the anticonvulsant of choice for eclampsia prevention and treatment.

steps.tx: The intramuscular regimen with loading doses into each buttock is the **Pritchard regimen**. It suits settings without infusion pumps, needing only clinical monitoring of reflexes, respiration and urine. Maintenance doses follow every four hours while criteria stay safe. Correlating this finding with imaging and laboratory results prevents both delayed treatment and unnecessary intervention in most patients.
steps.say: The Pritchard regimen uses intramuscular magnesium where infusion pumps are unavailable.

steps.tx: The continuous intravenous infusion regimen is the **Zuspan regimen**. A loading dose precedes a gram per hour infusion, typically for twenty four hours after delivery or the last fit. Serum levels are checked when renal function is impaired. Early recognition matters because timely treatment gives clearly better outcomes than waiting for complications to develop first.
steps.say: The Zuspan regimen infuses a gram per hour for twenty four hours after delivery.

steps.tx: Loss of deep tendon reflexes is the earliest clinical sign of magnesium excess, monitored through the **patellar reflex**. Each maintenance dose requires reflexes present, breathing adequate and urine flowing. Any failure withholds the dose. Students should connect this fact with the presenting symptoms, since examination questions usually test that clinical link directly.
steps.say: The patellar reflex is checked before every magnesium dose as the earliest toxicity sign.

steps.tx: The specific antidote reversing magnesium toxicity is **calcium gluconate**. One gram given intravenously over minutes restores neuromuscular function. It is drawn up and kept at the bedside during magnesium therapy. Documenting this finding clearly in the notes guides the next clinician and supports safe, well planned further management.
steps.say: Calcium gluconate reverses magnesium toxicity and is kept at the bedside throughout therapy.

steps.tx: Magnesium also protects the preterm fetal brain when given before early delivery, termed **neuroprotection**. Below thirty two weeks it reduces cerebral palsy in survivors. The same infusion serves mother and fetus simultaneously in pre-eclampsia. When this picture is seen in practice, urgent senior review is wise whenever there is any doubt about severity.
steps.say: Magnesium neuroprotection before preterm delivery reduces cerebral palsy in survivors.

steps.tx: Recurrent fit on magnesium is treated with a further bolus before changing drugs, following **breakthrough fit protocol**. Most eclamptic fits stop spontaneously within minutes. Airway, oxygen and left lateral positioning accompany drug therapy. Understanding this mechanism explains the symptoms, the investigation findings and the logic behind each step of treatment given.
steps.say: Breakthrough fits get a further magnesium bolus with airway and lateral positioning.

steps.tx: Renal impairment accumulates magnesium dangerously, demanding **dose adjustment in renal failure**. Serum levels guide therapy when urine output falls. Dialysis removes magnesium in life threatening toxicity. This distinction changes management, so it should be settled early rather than after empirical treatment has already begun.
steps.say: Renal failure accumulates magnesium dangerously and demands level guided dosing.

steps.tx: Blood pressure itself is controlled separately with labetalol, hydralazine or nifedipine because magnesium is a poor antihypertensive, a distinction of **separate pressure control**. Severe hypertension needs treatment within the hour to prevent stroke. Magnesium continues alongside for seizure protection. Careful history taking and examination help place this finding in the right clinical context before treatment is planned.
steps.say: Separate pressure control treats severe hypertension because magnesium barely lowers pressure.
